keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1946-1975 row (477,476 km2) is the Territory of Papua and New Guinea under Australia, not a state: the page has the 'administrative union' of Papua and New Guinea on 1 July 1949 and independence on 16 September 1975. It also misses 91 cells of the modern country (all of Bougainville, 36 cells, and parts of New Ireland, New Britain and Milne Bay); 31 of them sit in Australia's 1946 row, the rest in no row. Do not draw it as Papua New Guinea before 1975; the Australian dossier carries the whole land as keyframes commonwealth-of-australia_1946.

483,568 km2 against the infobox 462,840 km2 (ratio 1.04), within coastal noise. The shape misses 74 cells of small islands the Natural Earth country has and takes 26 cells beyond its coast. Bougainville (North Solomons) is in the shape through 1976-2023 although the BRA held most of it from 1990 to 1997 (ledger).
Same shape as 1976; no change in the page since.

ledger.note: 1975: Papua New Guinea becomes independent from Australia. 'Setting 16 September 1975 as the date of independence'; self-government had begun on 1 December 1973, the 'administrative union' of Papua and New Guinea on 1 July 1949. The Territory pages give 15 September.

region.text: Bougainville apart from Buka, held by the Bougainville Revolutionary Army from 1990

ledger.note: 1990: the PNG forces leave Bougainville. 'In early 1990 Papua New Guinea withdrew, leaving Bougainville in the control of the BRA'; 'Francis Ona ... unilaterally declared independence in May 1990'; 'By the end of 1990, the PNGDF national forces controlled Buka, while the BRA controlled the remainder of Bougainville.' A blockade followed.

region.text: the north and southwest of the main island, retaken by 1991-92

ledger.note: 1991: PNG begins to retake the island. 'By 1991-92 [PNG] had retaken the north and southwest of the main island'; the blockade lasted to the 1994 ceasefire and informally to 1997. The page gives no month and no exact zones, so the whole province is the contest zone.

region.text: Arawa, the main town of Bougainville

ledger.note: 1993: PNG retakes Arawa. 'PNG retook Arawa in February 1993'; by 1996 it held 'roughly 40% of the island with resistance forces'.

1997: the fighting stops. 'Talks in mid-1997 produced a truce'; 'since then a ceasefire has largely held'; the Lincoln Agreement followed in January 1998. The BIG kept de facto control of its part of the island until the peace agreement.

region.text: Bougainville, then the Autonomous Region of Bougainville

ledger.note: 2001: Bougainville returns to PNG authority as an autonomous region. 'A peace agreement was reached in 2001'; PNG's page: 'The Bougainville Peace Agreement was signed in 2001, under which Bougainville would gain higher autonomy than other provinces'; the first Autonomous Bougainville Government was elected in May and June 2005; in the 23 November 2019 referendum 98.31% voted for independence (non-binding).

wars.name: Bougainville Civil War

zones.text: Bougainville: the BRA held all but Buka at the end of 1990; PNG retook the north and southwest by 1991-92 and Arawa in February 1993

wars.outcome: A truce in mid-1997 and the Lincoln Agreement of January 1998; the Bougainville Peace Agreement of 2001 gave autonomy; first Autonomous Bougainville Government elected in 2005.
wars.note: Infobox start 1 December 1988 ('tensions over the mine led to local violence'). On 1 September 1975 'the government of Bougainville itself declared independence' (Papua New Guinea page); the page opened does not say how long it lasted, so it is not entered as a contest.

certainty.note: Land border with Indonesia to the west; island coasts.
Bougainville: de facto BRA/BIG control, PNG holding Buka and by 1996 about 40% of the island.
Bougainville is an autonomous region from the 2001 agreement, still inside the PNG border.

notes:
Written 2026-10-18 from two pages (budget 1-2). Cliopatria's Papua New Guinea row runs 1946-2024, but the page dates the state to independence on 16 September 1975; the 1946 shape (Territory of Papua and New Guinea) is declared wrong as a state and its land is carried by commonwealth-of-australia (keyframes 1920 and 1946 there). Disagreement between pages: independence is 16 September 1975 on the Papua New Guinea page, 15 September on the Territory of Papua and Territory of New Guinea pages; the mandate for New Guinea is 9 or 19 May 1921 here but 17 December 1920 on the Territory of New Guinea page.

Rebel state: bougainville-interim-government (BRA/BIG) is written as a type rebel dossier from the same two pages. The page does not give the day of the May 1990 declaration or the withdrawal of PNG forces ('early 1990'), nor the capital of the BIG. The 1 September 1975 Bougainville declaration (before PNG's independence) is mentioned on the Papua New Guinea page without end date or name, so it has no ledger event; a gap-filler should open 'Republic of the North Solomons' if a page exists.

Gazetteer: 'Buka' (island north of Bougainville, about 25 km radius) is not in places.jsonl; Arawa is. Cliopatria's shape covers Bougainville throughout 1976-2023 (the BRA-held years are in the ledger, not in the keyframes). The shape also touches Indonesian cells at the 141 E border (modern_countries lists Indonesia): coastal-cell noise, left as ok. The 'wrong' verdict on the 1946 row is a judgment about status (territory, not state): if the project prefers colonies drawn under their own name, the alternative is to keep the row as a type colony tinted by Australia; the Australian dossier then must not also hold the land directly.
